title: British, American & Australian English

expressions.example: Long day? Fancy a cuppa before we start?
Thanks for the lift! — No worries, mate.
After that twelve-hour shift, I'm absolutely knackered.

expressions.expr: Two nations divided by a common language
expressions.meaning: Duas nações separadas pela mesma língua (sobre EUA e Reino Unido)
expressions.example: When my London friend laughed at the word 'pants', I understood the saying about two nations divided by a common language.

sentences: In London we took the underground, but in New York everyone said subway.
I've just finished my homework, as a British speaker would say; an American might say 'I just finished it'.
The team are playing well tonight, said the British commentator.
In Sydney, my host asked if I wanted brekkie before we went to the beach.
Could we have the bill, please? — or, in the United States, the check.
She's got two brothers, but her American cousin says she has two brothers.
I reckon the Australian accent is easier to understand than people think.
Don't worry about the spelling: colour and color are both correct, depending on where you are.

grammar.title: US vs UK Grammar Differences
rules: Present perfect: britânicos usam mais com just/already/yet ('I've just eaten'); americanos aceitam o past simple ('I just ate').
Posse: 'have got' é muito comum no Reino Unido ('I've got a car'); nos EUA o normal é 'have' ('I have a car').
Substantivos coletivos: no Reino Unido 'the team are' é comum (pensa nas pessoas); nos EUA é sempre 'the team is'.
Preposições mudam: 'at the weekend' (UK) x 'on the weekend' (US); 'different to' (UK) x 'different than' (US).

quiz.q: What is a 'lift' in British English?
quiz.why: Lift (UK) = elevator (US). Em inglês americano, 'lift' é mais usado como carona.

quiz.q: An American asks for the 'check' at a restaurant. What does a British person say?
quiz.why: Na mesa do restaurante: bill (UK) = check (US).
'Have got' para posse é marca do inglês britânico.
Arvo é a gíria australiana para afternoon.

quiz.q: Choose the American option: 'I'll see you ___ the weekend.'
quiz.why: Nos EUA: on the weekend. No Reino Unido: at the weekend.

speak: I've just finished, but my American friend says I just finished.
Could we have the bill, please?
Fancy a cuppa before the meeting?
No worries, mate, see you this arvo.
I reckon both accents are brilliant.
